assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mesoscopic nanocrystalline TiO2 films sensitised by molecular dyes created a new, clearly conceived class of photovoltaic device in which structure (high internal surface area, interpenetrating electrolyte) directly sets function. The concept opened an entire field of photoelectrochemistry and set the stage for later solution-processed solar cells; impact on both science and technology is lasting.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 Nature paper by O'Regan and Grätzel is the decisive contribution, with Grätzel the sustained intellectual leader of the field. Hagfeldt is an important later contributor and developer but not the originator, so a two-person configuration is the cleanest from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of independent confirmation, commercial and pilot-scale modules, and a stable interpretation of the mechanism make recognition fully timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to credit O'Regan alongside Grätzel or Grätzel alone; relative weight of Hagfeldt's later contributions is uncertain.
Practical efficiency and stability limits of the dye cells themselves, now partly overtaken by perovskites.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (M41S, MCM-41) extended the pore range of molecular sieves beyond zeolites and demonstrated true supramolecular templating of inorganic frameworks. This is a structural and synthetic breakthrough with broad impact in catalysis, adsorption, separation and later hard-templating of other materials; closely tied to the porous-framework tradition recognised in recent prizes.
assessment.attribution: The Mobil discovery of M41S by Kresge, Beck and co-workers in 1992 is the clear origin; Stucky, Ryoo, Zhao and Inagaki (and Kuroda's earlier FSM-16 work, outside the supplied names) were major followers and extenders. A fair configuration is the Mobil pair, though the priority question regarding FSM-16 and Mobil co-inventors is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation, standard characterisation by XRD, TEM and sorption, wide industrial and academic uptake; some initial promise in industrial catalysis was only partly realised, but scientific impact is mature.
uncertainties: Credit for Mobil co-inventors beyond the two named and for the earlier Japanese work; commercial impact of mesoporous silica is more modest than for zeolites.
Only two of the many contributors can be selected and this omits Stucky, Ryoo, Zhao and Inagaki.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced one of the fastest rises in photovoltaic efficiency, from a few percent to over 25 percent in about a decade, through a simple solution-processed crystalline material. The scientific impact on semiconductor chemistry, defect tolerance and tandem devices is large and the application relevance to energy is obvious.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka's 2009 sensitised cells, Park's 2011-2012 improvement and Snaith's solid-state devices and mixed-halide work are the decisive steps. Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel also made substantial contributions; any three-person split is contestable and Kojima is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is overwhelming for efficiency, but long-term operational stability, lead toxicity and commercialisation remain unresolved, so recognition may be somewhat premature compared with mature fields.
uncertainties: Stability and scale-up are not yet settled, which weakens lasting-impact arguments.
Attribution is crowded and the first-reported device by Kojima is not among the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity degradation of proteins by PROTACs and molecular glues created a new therapeutic modality, with the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism explaining a long-standing drug puzzle. The concept is original and clinical translation is now underway, though mostly outside my own field.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs, Ciulli contributed VHL-based structural design, and Handa identified cereblon as thalidomide's target. The credit divides between the PROTAC concept and the molecular-glue mechanism, a compound discovery whose parts may need different recognition.
assessment.maturity: The mechanistic work is well confirmed and the first clinical results are encouraging, but approved degrader drugs are still few so impact is still developing.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should recognise PROTACs, molecular glues, or both, and the many contributors (Deshaies, Gray, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim).
Clinical validation is incomplete and my expertise in chemical biology is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one DNA base to another without double-strand breaks by tethering deaminases to a programmable Cas protein. It is an elegant chemistry-driven engineering advance that has reached clinical trials and complements the 2020 CRISPR prize.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory was decisive for both cytosine and adenine base editing, with Komor and Gaudelli as the lead first authors; Nishida and Kondo reported independent related cytidine editing. Liu is the clear intellectual leader, and the extent of the trainee credit is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, widespread laboratory use and early clinical evidence; rapid but credible maturity, with the broader gene-editing context already recognised in 2020.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier CRISPR prize and with prime editing, which could favour a combined Liu recognition.
Priority of Nishida and Kondo versus Komor on cytidine editing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and related molecular sieves, including organic structure-directing agents, new frameworks and engineered active sites, underpins refining, emissions control and selective catalysis. Structure determines function here, which matches my own interests, and the lasting industrial impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Zones (structure-directing agents, SSZ-13 for NOx), Corma (zeolite catalysis and new frameworks) and Davis (design of molecular sieves and active sites) are the strongest candidates; Yu and Tsapatsis are also leaders. This is a field-wide achievement rather than one discovery, and defining a sharp prize citation is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed and industrially proven for decades, so timeliness is not a concern; the main difficulty is the diffuse scope.
uncertainties: The discovery is broad and the citation may be unclear; there is also my own closeness to the zeolite field, which could bias judgement.
Allocation among Zones, Corma, Davis, Yu and Tsapatsis is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Supported single-atom catalysts push heterogeneous catalysis to the limit of atomic efficiency and link homogeneous and heterogeneous concepts. Their identification depends on aberration-corrected electron microscopy and XAS, so the claim is structural, and the field has grown enormously.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Qiao, Wang, Zhang (Pt1/FeOx) paper coined the concept and is widely credited; Jingyue Liu contributed early STEM identification of isolated atoms. Datye and Li contributed to stability and theory. Credit is not cleanly separable because earlier isolated-atom observations exist.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing but still young; many reports suffer from ambiguous structural assignment and the practical advantage over nanoparticle catalysts is still debated, so the prize may be premature.
uncertainties: Rigour of structural proof of single-atom sites in many reports, and real stability under working conditions.
Priority relative to earlier atomically dispersed catalysts and which three names are fairest.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enabled structure determination from nanocrystals and time-resolved studies of molecular dynamics, with a diffraction-before-destruction principle. As a crystallographer I value this enabling method, which parallels the use of electron diffraction for tiny crystals.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 proof of principle with Fromme, Hajdu and Schlichting among the central contributors, with Neutze's work on diffraction before destruction outside the supplied names. The group is large and a three-person configuration omits Schlichting and others.
assessment.maturity: Method is validated and now routine at several facilities, although the unique chemical discoveries it produced are fewer than hoped and depend on a few large facilities.
uncertainties: Whether the method has yielded sufficiently important new chemistry to merit a prize at this time.
The Hajdu contribution is posthumous and the exact allocation among the credited names is unresolved.
